reason: 'not connate' = like parts not fused: negation of FLOPO:0991067 connate. FLOPO:0991068 free says more (not fused to anything compared), so the plain negation is the safer reading.
Negation of FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped, added in the previous review; said of branches and sepals as in its bearer list.
'Minutely pimpled' testa, blade and fruit = bearing small rounded or nipple-like projections, the definition of FLOPO:0991059 papillose. Coarser tubercles would be FLOPO:0991060 tuberculate.
The previous review maps 'pitted' to PATO:0002296 foveate (rule C179); 'pitless' / 'without pits' is its negation. PO has no pit class for an absence rule.
A pseudoraceme is an inflorescence that looks like a raceme but whose units are reduced cymes or fascicles. That is exactly a raceme-like architecture, FLOPO:0991197.

'Covered with glands' states that glands are present (gland is a RELATED synonym of PO:0005656, rule C265). PATO:0002117 glandular means gland-like, not gland-bearing. When the glands are said to be stalked, FLOPO:0991172 stipitate-glandular applies.
'Bamboo' names a group of grasses (the habit of the taxon itself), not a quality of the whole plant. Unlike palm-like it is not used as a comparison with other plants.

label: coralloid
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being much and shortly branched, with thick, blunt branch tips, like a coral. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991128 anastomosing; used of the coralloid roots of cycads, of outgrowths and of bark.
reason: Coralloid is an established botanical term (cycad roots, outgrowths) with no PATO or FLOPO counterpart. 'Coral-like pubescence' is a looser use.

Apiculate (ending abruptly in a short point) has no value term: PATO lists 'apiculate' only as an EXACT synonym of the attribute PATO:0000944 sharpness. The nearest value is FLOPO:0991054 mucronate; 'bluntly' is a degree that is not represented.
Not a quality: 'partial inflorescences' and 'partial rhachis' name subordinate parts, and 'hyalodermis partial' is extent without a reference.

label: lithophytic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing on rock surfaces or in rock crevices rather than in soil. NOTE: Probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives); kept beside FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic and FLOPO:0991111 terrestrial; the phenotype class FLOPO_0980082 whole plant litophytic should use it.
reason: Habitat-position quality of the same kind as epiphytic and terrestrial, which were added as FLOPO values. It is contrasted with 'terrestrial' in the examples.
'Of equal size', 'de même taille' = members of a set of like parts having the same size: FLOPO:0991102 equal.
Interlacing bark ridges, furrows and veins form a network: FLOPO:0991100 reticulate. 'Interlacing branches/trunks' (intertwined stems) is a different sense and should not take this rule.

As 'obscure' (rule C174) and 'nerved' (rule C212): the veins (vascular bundle PO:0005020) of the bearer are present but not clearly visible. The quality inheres in the veins as a part of the bearer (pattern 04 part slot).

label: persistent
definition: A shedability quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's remaining attached to the plant after it has ceased to function or after the time when such structures are usually shed. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0001731 deciduous (plant) and FLOPO:0991181 marcescent; PATO has only the attribute PATO:0000082 persistence.
reason: 'Retained leaf-bases' = persistent leaf bases, a common botanical quality with no value term. 'Cotyledons remaining in the seed' is hypogeal germination, a different sense that should not take this rule.
vein is an EXACT synonym of vascular bundle; 'midvein' and '0-3-veined' are read as the part, with counts going to pattern 03.

Mixed and vague: 'croissance limitée' (determinate growth of a leaf or rachis), 'very little lateral growth' of roots and an inflorescence 'quite limited'. FLOPO:0991034 indeterminate is defined for inflorescences only.

'Not septate' anthers and fruits = without partitions: complement of has_part some septum (anther septum PO:0005010 and fruit septum PO:0025268 are its children). PATO lists septate only as a NARROW synonym of split, which does not fit.
PATO:0001981 auriculate is defined as having a shape resembling an ear; 'auriculiforme' and 'ear-shaped glands' match.
'Deeply penetrating taproot' states rooting depth in the soil, an ecological statement without a measure, not a quality of the root.
Negation of FLOPO:0991138 buttressed, said of the trunk or whole plant.
A fragment of colour words such as 'mid- to dark green'. The shade belongs with the colour (botanical colour synonyms, continuum of two values), not as a quality of its own.

'Thorn-like branchlets' and 'thorn-like tips' of branches are branches modified into thorns, the part PO:0025172. 'Spine thorn-like' and 'thorn-like nodules' are other senses and should be left unmapped.
A compound of two shape values, PATO:0000946 oblong and PATO:0001936 obovate, read like 'linear-lanceolate'. 'Broadly' is a width modifier and does not need a term.
A compound of two margin values: PATO:0001889 scalloped (synonym crenulate) and PATO:0001206 serrated.
'Darkening to pink', 'darkening at the tips' is a change of colour over time or towards a region, the transition pattern ('white becoming pink'), not a quality.
distorted is a RELATED synonym of PATO:0001617 deformed. 'Distorted on drying' also takes the specimen-condition pattern 06.

'Diverse in shape / de coloration diverse' = varying within the taxon: PATO:0001227 variant (synonym variable), or its children PATO:0001930 variant shape and PATO:0001515 variable color when the attribute is named.
A compound of PATO:0001154 elongated and the oval outline, which botanically is PATO:0000947 elliptic. PATO's 'oval' synonym under ovate should not be used for it.
A fig is pyriform: broad and rounded above, narrowed to the base. 'Fig-shaped or obovoid' fruits and perianths match PATO:0005002 pear shaped.
